To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
both HNF4 and C/EP beta are required for the enhancers of liver-specific genes to activate transcription in a liver-selective manner.

the liver-selective transcription factor HNF-4 is necessary but insufficient for liver-specific activation of the OTC enhancer, that the liver-selectivity of this enhancer is conferred by combinatorial activation of HNF-4 by the second liver-selective transcriptional activator C/EBP, and that the liver specificity of the enhancers can be inverted by inactivating either of the HNF-4 or the C/EBP sites.

the enhancer of the ornithinetranscarbamylase (OTC) gene is capable of inverting the tissue-specificity of the homologousoverlapping promoter and that the enhancer contains two liver-selective transcription factor-binding sites, one for hepatocyte nuclear factors (HNFs) and one for CCAAT/ enhancer binding proteins (C/EBPs), and that both HNFs and C/EBPs are required for the enhancereactivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanisms underlying the tissue specificity of transcriptional regulation.
the mechanism by which tissue-enriched but not strictly tissue-specific transcription factors can confer tissue specificity on transcription of the target genes.

the mechanism of tissue-specific gene transcription, and our results provide an example of how the liver-specificity of transcription can be determined by the combinatorial operation, in a tissue-restricted manner, of tissue-enrichment factors that are not liver specific themselves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tissue specificity of a gene can be determined by combinatorial action of tissue-enriching transcription factors, and the number and type of these factors are dependent on the target gene and the tissue in which the gene is to be activated.
the liver-specificity of the enhancer is achieved by a combination of two factors, HNF-4, and C/EBPs.

the enhancer of the OTC gene is a liver-specific enhancer, but that the tissue specificity of this enhancer is determined by the combinatorial operation and the concentration of two tissue-enriched factors, HNF-4, and C/EBPs, both of which are necessary and sufficient to confer liver-specific transcriptional activity to a heterologous promoter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tissue specificity of a gene is determined by a combinatorial operation, in which a number of transcription factors, which are enriched in a particular tissue, are involved.
the liver specificity of the enhancers is determined by the number and the types of transcription factors required for the enhancers to function.

the liver-specific transcription factor is a complex of at least two tissue-enriched factors, and that the tissue specificity of a transcription unit is determined by combinatorial operations of such tissue-enriched but not strictly tissue-specific factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver-specific transcriptional activation by the enhancer is achieved by combinatorial operations of two liver-enrichal transcription factors.
combinatorial action of multiple tissue-enriched factors can determine the tissue specificity of transcription.
the liver-selective transcription factor HNF-4, when combined with another liver-enriched factor C/EBP, confers liver specificity on the target gene.
